name: drone_a2_sensors
description: Downward-biased elevation window for approach/landing traffic (issue #7). The shipped 20 deg symmetric FOV can only follow a height difference of r*tan(10) ~= 0.18r, so an aircraft on final approach leaves the window exactly when it matters -- close in and below. Elevation is opened to 45 deg placed ASYMMETRICALLY at -35..+10, because the sector that matters below the horizon is far larger than the one above it. points_per_second is raised by the same 2.25x span ratio: PointsPerScan() does not depend on the window, so widening it alone would spread the same rays over more sky and make the radar LESS sensitive (measured: 1751 -> 799 returns on a fixed target, restored to 1779 by the compensation). COST, measured with a floor in the sensing world at a 1.2 m cruise height: ground returns go from 49 to 237 per frame and the nearest one from 6.33 m to 1.91 m. All of it is static, so a moving-target filter removes it while the aircraft HOVERS -- but not while it flies: ground 30 deg below a radar moving at 1 m/s closes at 0.87 m/s, which no sane threshold rejects. Use this fit over terrain only with that in mind; over an empty sensing world (two_drone_run.sh noground, the S-5 default) there is no cost at all.
